words.enDefinition: to stay informed about what is happening in friends' lives

examples.en: I find it easier to keep up with friends when we send short messages.
examples.zh: 我们发简短的消息时，我更容易「了解朋友的近况」。

examples.en: My summer shifts meant I could only keep up with friends on Sundays.
examples.zh: 暑假排班让我只能在周日「了解朋友的近况」。

collocations: try to keep up with friends
find time to keep up with friends
keep up with friends from home

words.enDefinition: to contact someone briefly in writing, in informal speech

examples.en: You can drop someone a line if you want to ask how they are.
examples.zh: 想问对方过得怎样，可以「给某人发个简短消息」。

examples.en: It was easy to drop someone a line between classes on my new campus.
examples.zh: 在我现在的校区，两节课之间「给人发个简短消息」很方便。

collocations: remember to drop someone a line
drop me a line when you arrive

words.enDefinition: an informal invitation to contact you when the other person wants or needs to

examples.en: “Give me a shout when you're back on campus,” my friend said on Sunday.
examples.zh: 周日朋友说：“回到校园后「联系我一声」。”

examples.en: “Give me a shout if you need help with the move next weekend.”
examples.zh: “下周末搬家需要帮忙的话，「就联系我」。”

collocations: give me a shout if you need help
give me a shout when you're free

words.enDefinition: to contact a friend to find out whether they are all right

examples.en: I went upstairs to check in on a friend after she missed our usual coffee.
examples.zh: 朋友没来和我们像平时那样喝咖啡，我就上楼「问候朋友是否安好」。

examples.en: It's worth making time to check in on a friend during a busy exam week.
examples.zh: 考试周虽然忙，也可以抽点时间「问候朋友是否安好」。

collocations: take time to check in on a friend
remember to check in on a friend
call to check in on a friend

words.enDefinition: a phone call to hear someone's news since you last spoke

examples.en: We had a catch-up call on Friday after I finished my afternoon classes.
examples.zh: 周五，我上完下午的课后打了通「聊近况的电话」。

examples.en: Our first catch-up call after graduation lasted longer than either of us expected.
examples.zh: 毕业后第一次「聊近况的电话」比我们两人预想的都久。

words.enDefinition: an informal expression saying a long time has passed since something happened

examples.en: “It's been ages since we last saw each other,” she said outside the library.
examples.zh: 在图书馆外她说：“我们上次见面到现在「已经好久了」。”

examples.en: I smiled and said, “It's been ages,” when my old classmate sat beside me.
examples.zh: 老同学在我旁边坐下时，我笑着说：“「好久没见了」。”

collocations: it's been ages since we met
it's been ages since we spoke

words.expression: pick up where we left off
words.lemma: pick up where we left off
words.zhGloss: 从上次停下的地方接下去
words.enDefinition: to continue an earlier activity or conversation from the point it stopped
acceptedZhAnswers: 从上次停下的地方接下去
acceptedEnVariants: pick up where we left off

examples.en: At the reunion, we found we could pick up where we left off.
examples.zh: 重聚时，我们发现自己还能「像从前那样聊下去」。

examples.en: We decided to pick up where we left off after comparing our new class schedules.
examples.zh: 对过新的课表后，我们决定「从上次停下的地方接下去」。

collocations: easily pick up where we left off
agree to pick up where we left off
ready to pick up where we left off

words.enDefinition: to have known each other for a long time, in informal speech

examples.en: My cousin and I go way back with the neighbours who used to live downstairs.
examples.zh: 我和表亲都跟以前住楼下的邻居「很早就认识了」。

examples.en: You can tell they go way back from the stories they share over dinner.
examples.zh: 听两人晚饭时讲的那些故事，就知道他们「很早就认识了」。

words.enDefinition: a friend someone has known for a long period

examples.en: I stayed with a longtime friend when I went back for a campus reunion.
examples.zh: 我返校参加聚会时，住在一位「相识多年的朋友」家里。

examples.en: A longtime friend sent a postcard from the city where we first studied together.
examples.zh: 一位「相识多年的朋友」从我们最初一起读书的城市寄来了一张明信片。

words.enDefinition: a friend who remains close through much or all of one's life

examples.en: She never expected her neighbour in first-year residence to become a lifelong friend.
examples.zh: 她没想到大一住隔壁的人会成为「一辈子的朋友」。

examples.en: The first person to call after my graduation was a lifelong friend from home.
examples.zh: 毕业后第一个打来电话的是老家一位「一辈子的朋友」。

words.enDefinition: someone you became friends with when you attended school together

examples.en: A school friend came to visit me during my last week on campus.
examples.zh: 在学校的最后一周，一位「上学时认识的朋友」来看我。

examples.en: I shared the wedding photo with a school friend who still knew both families.
examples.zh: 我把婚礼照片发给一位「上学时认识的朋友」，对方至今还认识两家人。

words.enDefinition: someone who used to be in one of your classes

examples.en: I ran into an old classmate outside the library on my way to work.
examples.zh: 上班路上，我在图书馆外碰到了一位「老同学」。

examples.en: An old classmate helped me remember the name of the teacher in that photograph.
examples.zh: 一位「老同学」帮我想起了那张照片里老师的名字。

words.enDefinition: a friend made at university, especially in informal British and Australian English

examples.en: I met a uni friend for lunch while I was visiting Bristol again.
examples.zh: 又去布里斯托那次，我和一位「大学里认识的朋友」一起吃了午饭。

examples.en: A uni friend in Sydney offered me a place to stay after the reunion.
examples.zh: 聚会结束后，一位在悉尼「大学里认识的朋友」主动让我在他那儿留宿。

collocations: meet up with a uni friend

words.enDefinition: friends from the place where someone lived before moving away

examples.en: I called my friends from back home the evening before my first university lecture.
examples.zh: 大学第一节课前一晚，我给「老家的朋友们」打了电话。

examples.en: My friends from back home kept asking to see pictures of the new city.
examples.zh: 「老家的朋友们」一直让我发新城市的照片给他们看。

collocations: hear from friends from back home

words.enDefinition: a small group of the people someone trusts or spends most time with

examples.en: Only her inner circle knew she was thinking of changing universities that year.
examples.zh: 只有她「最亲近的小圈子」里的人知道，她那年在考虑转学。

examples.en: He invited his inner circle to a small lunch before leaving for his placement.
examples.zh: 动身去实习前，他请「最亲近的小圈子」一起简单吃了顿午饭。

words.enDefinition: a group whose members know each other well and support one another

examples.en: Our year abroad turned four strangers into a close-knit group by the final month.
examples.zh: 到最后一个月，那一年的留学经历让四个陌生人成了「关系紧密的群体」。

examples.en: It took time to feel at home in such a close-knit group of friends.
examples.zh: 在这样一个「关系紧密的」朋友圈里，我花了些时间才感觉自在。

words.enDefinition: the patterns in how members of a group of friends interact

examples.en: The move changed our friend group dynamics because two of us lived farther apart.
examples.zh: 搬家改变了「朋友圈里的相处模式」，因为我们中有两个人住远了。

examples.en: She noticed different friend group dynamics after several classmates joined the weekly club meeting.
examples.zh: 几个同学开始参加每周的社团聚会后，她注意到「朋友圈里的相处模式」变了。

collocations: notice changes in friend group dynamics

words.enDefinition: to continue a friendship through sustained contact or shared effort

examples.en: It took more effort to maintain a friendship once we stopped sharing a timetable.
examples.zh: 不再共用一份课表后，「维系一段友情」要花更多心思。

examples.en: They found it easy to maintain a friendship even while studying in separate cities.
examples.zh: 即使在不同城市读书，他们也觉得「维系一段友情」并不难。

words.enDefinition: a friendship maintained by people who live far apart

examples.en: Our long-distance friendship began when we went to universities in different countries.
examples.zh: 到不同国家读大学后，我们开始维系这段「异地友情」。

examples.en: The long-distance friendship mattered as much to her as the friendships on her course.
examples.zh: 这段「异地友情」对她来说和同一门课上的友情同样重要。

words.enDefinition: friends who live in places with different local times

examples.en: My friends across time zones agreed on a call before our classes started again.
examples.zh: 我和「身处不同时区的朋友」约好开课前打一次电话。

examples.en: It took a while to find a regular meeting time for friends across time zones.
examples.zh: 给「身处不同时区的朋友」找到固定碰面的时间花了好一阵。

collocations: stay close to friends across time zones
make time for friends across time zones

words.enDefinition: repeated brief contact to ask how someone is doing

examples.en: Our regular check-in made it easier to notice when someone was having a hard week.
examples.zh: 「定期联络问候」让我们更容易留意到谁这周过得比较困难。

examples.en: We had a regular check-in over coffee until my friend moved to another city.
examples.zh: 在朋友搬去另一座城之前，我们一直一起喝咖啡「定期联络问候」。

collocations: make time for a regular check-in

words.enDefinition: a phone or video conversation arranged to happen once a week

examples.en: Our weekly call moved to Monday because her lab now ran late on Fridays.
examples.zh: 她的实验课现在周五下课晚，我们把「每周一次的电话」改到周一。

examples.en: I missed the weekly call when my train was delayed outside the city.
examples.zh: 火车在城外延误了，我错过了「每周一次的电话」。

words.enDefinition: past experiences that people know about because they lived through them together

examples.en: Our shared history made it easy to talk after so many years apart.
examples.zh: 分开那么多年后，「共同经历过的往事」让我们很自然地聊了起来。

examples.en: The photos reminded us of the shared history behind our old university friendships.
examples.zh: 照片让我们想起了大学友情背后那些「共同经历过的往事」。

words.enDefinition: a joke or humorous idea repeated over time among the same people

examples.en: The missing umbrella became a running joke during the rest of our exchange year.
examples.zh: 丢掉的那把伞成了后来整个交换学年「反复被提起的玩笑」。

examples.en: We had a running joke about always choosing the wrong door at the library.
examples.zh: 我们老是选错图书馆的门，这事成了「反复被提起的玩笑」。

words.expression: take a trip down memory lane
words.lemma: take a trip down memory lane
words.enDefinition: to remember or talk about events from the past with pleasure
acceptedEnVariants: take a trip down memory lane

examples.en: We opened our old group photos to take a trip down memory lane after dinner.
examples.zh: 晚饭后，我们翻出小组旧照「一起回忆往事」。

examples.en: Some old classmates wanted to take a trip down memory lane before the reunion ended.
examples.zh: 聚会结束前，几位老同学想「一起回忆往事」。

collocations: take a trip down memory lane with friends
invite someone to take a trip down memory lane
take a trip down memory lane together

words.enDefinition: to think or talk with pleasure about something that happened in the past

examples.en: We stayed at the café to reminisce about the year we lived in residence.
examples.zh: 我们留在咖啡馆，「回味」一起住宿舍的那一年。

examples.en: My former classmates liked to reminisce about the trips we took during spring break.
examples.zh: 以前的同学喜欢「回味」我们春假那几次出游。

collocations: get together to reminisce about something

words.enDefinition: to cause someone to remember something from their own past

examples.en: Certain songs bring back memories of our first few weeks at university together.
examples.zh: 有些歌会「唤起我们刚上大学那几周的回忆」。

examples.en: The meal seemed to bring back memories for everyone who lived in that flat.
examples.zh: 对曾住那套公寓的人来说，这顿饭似乎会「唤起回忆」。

words.enDefinition: done to remember or enjoy something associated with a shared past

examples.en: We ordered our old favourite snack for old times' sake after the campus tour.
examples.zh: 参观完校园后，我们点了以前最喜欢的小吃，「为了重温旧日时光」。

examples.en: I suggested sitting in the old study room for old times' sake before leaving.
examples.zh: 离开前，我建议去老自习室坐一坐，「为了重温旧日时光」。

collocations: do something for old times' sake
go back for old times' sake

words.enDefinition: resembling a familiar, shared experience from the past

examples.en: We ended up talking until midnight again, like old times in our first year.
examples.zh: 我们又聊到了半夜，「就像大一时那样」。

examples.en: Walking home together after the lecture felt like old times to both of us.
examples.zh: 听完讲座一起走回家，两人感觉「就像从前一样」。

words.enDefinition: to keep a strong personal connection even as circumstances change

examples.en: We managed to stay close after we moved to opposite sides of the city.
examples.zh: 我们搬到城里相隔很远的两头后，关系还是「保持亲近」。

examples.en: She wanted to stay close to her old friends while making new ones abroad.
examples.zh: 她在国外交新朋友，也想和老朋友「继续保持亲近」。

words.enDefinition: to be willing to protect or support one another when needed

examples.en: We try to have each other's backs when either of us has a hard week.
examples.zh: 我们中间谁遇到难熬的一周，都会尽量「彼此照应」。

examples.en: They have each other's backs and take turns helping when one of them is busy.
examples.zh: 两人「彼此照应」，谁忙不过来，另一个就帮忙。

collocations: promise to have each other's backs
friends who have each other's backs

words.enDefinition: a bracelet given or exchanged as a symbol of friendship

examples.en: My former flatmate sent me a friendship bracelet after she moved abroad to study.
examples.zh: 以前的室友出国读书后，寄给我一条「友谊手链」。

examples.en: I found our friendship bracelet while looking through photos from my first year.
examples.zh: 翻看大一照片时，我找到了我们那条「友谊手链」。

words.enDefinition: to be present or make an effort when a friend needs support

examples.en: Sometimes the best way to show up for a friend is to listen quietly.
examples.zh: 有时「在朋友需要时出现」，只要安静地听对方说就好。

examples.en: She taught me what it meant to show up for a friend during exam week.
examples.zh: 考试那周，她让我明白了什么叫「在朋友需要时出现」。

collocations: find ways to show up for a friend
make time to show up for a friend
decide to show up for a friend

words.enDefinition: a person who gives you emotional or practical support when needed

examples.en: My old roommate was someone to lean on during the first difficult month abroad.
examples.zh: 刚出国最难的那个月，原来的室友是我「可以依靠的人」。

examples.en: It helped to have someone to lean on while I sorted out my university paperwork.
examples.zh: 处理学校手续时，有个「可以依靠的人」让我好过些。

words.enDefinition: a willingness to listen patiently and sympathetically to someone

examples.en: My neighbour offered a listening ear when I was worrying about a family decision.
examples.zh: 我正为家里的决定担心时，邻居「愿意听我倾诉」。

examples.en: I didn't need advice, but it helped to have a listening ear after class.
examples.zh: 我不需要建议，下课后有人「愿意听我倾诉」就很有帮助。

words.enDefinition: to initiate contact with a friend, especially to ask or offer support

examples.en: I decided to reach out to a friend after a week of studying alone.
examples.zh: 一个人学了一周后，我决定「主动联系一位朋友」。

examples.en: She made time to reach out to a friend who had just started university.
examples.zh: 她抽时间「主动联系一位刚上大学的朋友」。

collocations: decide to reach out to a friend
remember to reach out to a friend
time to reach out to a friend

words.zhGloss: 因各自成长而不再适合做朋友
words.enDefinition: to change over time until an old friendship no longer suits the people involved
acceptedZhAnswers: 因各自成长而不再适合做朋友

examples.en: She wondered whether people can outgrow a friendship without having a single argument.
examples.zh: 她想知道，两个人没吵过一次架，也会不会「因各自成长而不再适合做朋友」。

examples.en: Sometimes friends outgrow a friendship as their lives take them in different directions.
examples.zh: 有时候朋友走上不同的生活道路，会「因各自成长而不再适合做朋友」。

collocations: feel you may outgrow a friendship

words.enDefinition: to support someone and hope they do well, chiefly in North American English

examples.en: We went to the student debate to root for someone from our residence hall.
examples.zh: 我们去看学生辩论，为同宿舍楼的人「打气」。

examples.en: It's easy to root for someone who has worked so hard on a project.
examples.zh: 看到对方为项目这么努力，很自然就想「为这个人打气」。

collocations: root for someone on the team

words.enDefinition: to encourage someone while they try to do something difficult or competitive

examples.en: I went to the track to cheer someone on during the last student race.
examples.zh: 最后一场学生赛跑时，我去了跑道边「给参赛者加油助威」。

examples.en: I stayed to cheer someone on through the last song of the campus contest.
examples.zh: 校园比赛唱到最后一首歌时，我还留在场边「给参赛者加油助威」。

collocations: cheer someone on from the sidelines
cheer someone on during a race

words.zhGloss: 愿意倾听和安慰你的人
words.enDefinition: a person who offers comfort when someone is sad or upset
acceptedZhAnswers: 愿意倾听和安慰你的人

examples.en: My roommate was a shoulder to cry on after I got some disappointing news.
examples.zh: 我收到让人失望的消息后，室友就是那个「愿意倾听和安慰我的人」。

examples.en: He said he could offer a shoulder to cry on after the difficult conversation.
examples.zh: 那次不好开口的谈话结束后，他说他「愿意听我诉苦并安慰我」。

collocations: need a shoulder to cry on
offer a shoulder to cry on
be a shoulder to cry on

words.enDefinition: to discuss a concern with someone you believe will handle it with care

examples.en: It can help to talk to someone you trust after a difficult week away from home.
examples.zh: 离家在外遇到难熬的一周，「找信任的人聊一聊」可能有帮助。

examples.en: She told me to talk to someone you trust if the situation got confusing.
examples.zh: 她对我说，如果事情变得让人摸不着头脑，可以「找信任的人聊一聊」。

collocations: take time to talk to someone you trust
try to talk to someone you trust
find a chance to talk to someone you trust

words.enDefinition: to be thoroughly familiar with someone's character, habits, and reactions

examples.en: You can know someone inside out and still be surprised by their career plans.
examples.zh: 即使「非常了解某人」，也可能对对方的职业计划感到意外。

examples.en: She said you don't need to know someone inside out to notice they're unhappy.
examples.zh: 她说，不用「非常了解某人」，也能注意到对方不开心。

collocations: seem to know someone inside out
feel you know someone inside out
claim to know someone inside out

words.enDefinition: to become someone another person can trust through your behaviour over time

examples.en: It often takes small promises kept over time to earn someone's trust in a friendship.
examples.zh: 朋友间往往要长期信守小承诺，才能「赢得对方的信任」。

examples.en: She thought listening carefully was one way to earn someone's trust after they had met.
examples.zh: 她觉得相识后认真听对方说话，是「赢得对方信任」的一种方式。

collocations: take time to earn someone's trust

words.enDefinition: to do something that causes someone no longer to trust you

examples.en: Sharing a private message can break someone's trust even if it was a mistake.
examples.zh: 即使是无意分享私信，也可能「辜负对方的信任」。

examples.en: He didn't mean to break someone's trust when he repeated what he had heard.
examples.zh: 他复述听来的话时，本没想「辜负对方的信任」。

collocations: never want to break someone's trust
avoid doing something that may break someone's trust

words.enDefinition: to avoid telling others information that someone wants to remain private

examples.en: My roommate asked whether I could keep a secret about her new job offer.
examples.zh: 室友问我能不能为她新拿到的工作机会「保守秘密」。

examples.en: I knew she could keep a secret, so I told her before our classmates.
examples.zh: 我知道她能「保守秘密」，就先告诉了她，没先告诉其他同学。

collocations: ask someone to keep a secret
be able to keep a secret

words.enDefinition: to tell someone new information about your own life

examples.en: We used the call to share personal news before talking about our university work.
examples.zh: 我们先借电话「分享个人近况」，再聊学校里的事。

examples.en: She chose to share personal news privately instead of posting it for everyone to see.
examples.zh: 她选择私下「分享个人近况」，没有发给所有人看。

collocations: decide where to share personal news
feel ready to share personal news

words.enDefinition: an informal assurance that you will support someone when they need you

examples.en: “I've got your back,” she said when I told her about my difficult meeting.
examples.zh: 我告诉她那场会议不好应付，她说：“「我会支持你」。”

examples.en: He texted, “I've got your back if you need help after the concert.”
examples.zh: 他发消息说：“音乐会结束后要帮忙的话，「我会支持你」。”

collocations: don't worry, I've got your back
I've got your back if anything changes
I've got your back on this

words.enDefinition: a phrase asking that something said remain private between the people talking

examples.en: “This is just between us for now,” he said before sharing his news.
examples.zh: 他先说“这事目前「只限咱俩知道」”，才讲了自己的消息。

examples.en: I hoped the conversation would stay just between us until I had spoken to everyone.
examples.zh: 我希望在跟每个人都说过之前，这段谈话「只限咱俩知道」。

words.zhGloss: 帮忙听取想法并给反馈的人
words.enDefinition: a person who listens to your ideas and offers feedback before you decide
acceptedZhAnswers: 帮忙听取想法并给反馈的人

examples.en: My old roommate became a sounding board when I considered switching to another degree.
examples.zh: 我考虑转读另一个学位时，以前的室友「听了我的想法并给了反馈」。

examples.en: I needed a sounding board before I sent that long message to our group.
examples.zh: 给我们小组发那条长消息前，我需要「有人听听我的想法并给些反馈」。

collocations: use someone as a sounding board

words.enDefinition: to pass on a polite greeting from the speaker to someone else

examples.en: “Please give my regards to your parents,” I said after our campus tour.
examples.zh: 参观完校园后，我说：“请「代我问候」你的父母。”

examples.en: I asked her to give my regards to the classmates I had not seen.
examples.zh: 我请她「代我问候」那些我还没见到的同学。

collocations: give my regards to your family

words.enDefinition: an informal request to pass your greeting to someone else

examples.en: “Say hi for me if you see Mei at the library,” he said.
examples.zh: 他说：“如果在图书馆看到小梅，「替我打声招呼」。”

examples.en: “Say hi for me when you visit our old neighbours next weekend,” I said.
examples.zh: 我说：“下周末去看以前的邻居时，「替我打声招呼」。”

collocations: say hi for me when you see them
say hi for me next time

words.enDefinition: to feel pleased about another person's good news or success

examples.en: It's possible to be happy for someone while still feeling disappointed about your own result.
examples.zh: 即使对自己的结果感到失望，你也可以「为别人感到高兴」。

examples.en: My friend reminded me that I could be happy for someone facing a different opportunity.
examples.zh: 朋友提醒我，可以「为获得不同机会的人感到高兴」。

collocations: learn to be happy for someone

words.enDefinition: to mark an achievement made by one of your friends

examples.en: We brought cake to celebrate a friend's success after she passed her final interview.
examples.zh: 朋友通过最后一轮面试后，我们带了蛋糕去「庆祝她取得成功」。

examples.en: It felt right to celebrate a friend's success at the end of a difficult year.
examples.zh: 艰难的一年结束后，应该「庆祝朋友取得成功」。

collocations: get together to celebrate a friend's success
plan to celebrate a friend's success
take time to celebrate a friend's success

words.enDefinition: help that people provide to one another rather than in only one direction

examples.en: Our mutual support made the first weeks at university feel much less overwhelming.
examples.zh: 我们的「相互支持」让刚上大学的那几周轻松了许多。

examples.en: The small friendship group was built on mutual support during a demanding course.
examples.zh: 课程要求很高，那几个朋友靠「相互支持」走到了一起。

words.enDefinition: a friendship where only one person makes much effort or provides support

examples.en: She felt it had become a one-sided friendship once she was always making the calls.
examples.zh: 每次都是她打电话，她觉得这成了「一方单向付出的友情」。

examples.en: I wondered whether I was in a one-sided friendship after several ignored invitations.
examples.zh: 几次邀约都没回音后，我怀疑这是不是段「一方单向付出的友情」。

words.enDefinition: to respond to a kind action, feeling, or effort with one of your own

examples.en: My neighbour brought soup last week, so I wanted to reciprocate with some bread.
examples.zh: 邻居上周送了汤，我想送点面包来「以同样的方式回应」。

examples.en: I noticed how my friends reciprocate when someone checks in after a difficult day.
examples.zh: 有人在他们忙完难熬的一天后发来问候，我留意到朋友会怎样「以同样的方式回应」。

words.enDefinition: to alternate responsibility for staying in contact or asking how people are

examples.en: We agreed to take turns checking in while both of us were studying abroad.
examples.zh: 我们约好两人都在国外读书的时候，「轮流主动联系问候」。

examples.en: It felt fairer to take turns checking in instead of leaving it to one friend.
examples.zh: 「轮流主动联系问候」感觉更公平，免得只靠一个朋友张罗。

collocations: decide to take turns checking in
agree to take turns checking in
remember to take turns checking in

words.enDefinition: to do something helpful for someone who previously helped you

examples.en: I offered to return the favour by carrying her books back to the library.
examples.zh: 我提出帮她把书送回图书馆，「回报她的人情」。

examples.en: He wanted to return the favour after we helped him move into the new flat.
examples.zh: 我们帮他搬进新公寓后，他想「回报人情」。

collocations: find a way to return the favour

words.enDefinition: to reserve time to talk with someone about what has happened since you last met

examples.en: We promised to make time to catch up before everyone left for summer.
examples.zh: 大家暑假离开前，我们答应「抽空聊聊近况」。

examples.en: I tried to make time to catch up with my school friends every month.
examples.zh: 我尽量每月和以前上学时的朋友「抽空聊聊近况」。

collocations: try to make time to catch up
promise to make time to catch up
always make time to catch up

words.enDefinition: a plan that remains in place without being arranged again each time

examples.en: We had a standing plan to meet for coffee on the first Friday of each month.
examples.zh: 我们有个「长期固定的约定」，每月第一个周五见面喝咖啡。

examples.en: I kept the standing plan in my calendar after my timetable changed in spring.
examples.zh: 春天课表调整后，我还是把「长期固定的约定」留在日历里。

words.expression: keep a date in the diary
words.lemma: keep a date in the diary
words.enDefinition: to leave an agreed meeting on the calendar despite changing plans
acceptedEnVariants: keep a date in the diary

examples.en: We managed to keep a date in the diary through our busiest exam weeks.
examples.zh: 即使最忙的考试周，我们也设法「让约定留在日程上」。

examples.en: To keep a date in the diary, we picked one evening everyone could protect.
examples.zh: 为了「让约定留在日程上」，我们选了一个大家都能留空的晚上。

collocations: try to keep a date in the diary
agree to keep a date in the diary
find a way to keep a date in the diary

words.enDefinition: to start doing an enjoyable activity together repeatedly

examples.en: Our walk was so relaxing that we decided to make it a regular thing.
examples.zh: 散步太放松了，我们决定「把它变成固定活动」。

examples.en: “Should we make it a regular thing after class?” I asked over lunch.
examples.zh: 吃午饭时我问：“课后要不要「把它变成固定活动」？”

collocations: decide to make it a regular thing
agree to make it a regular thing
want to make it a regular thing

words.zhGloss: 朋友之间固定的小习惯
words.enDefinition: a small, repeated practice that a group of friends uses to stay connected
acceptedZhAnswers: 朋友之间固定的小习惯

examples.en: Our last coffee before each term break became a friendship ritual that everyone looked forward to.
examples.zh: 每次放假前喝最后一杯咖啡，成了大家盼着做的「朋友之间固定的小习惯」。

examples.en: Sending a photo from the station became a friendship ritual on our way home.
examples.zh: 每次回家路上从车站互发照片，成了「朋友之间固定的小习惯」。

words.expression: we should do this more often
words.lemma: we should do this more often
words.enDefinition: an expression suggesting that a shared activity should happen more frequently
acceptedEnVariants: we should do this more often

examples.en: “We should do this more often,” she said after our walk through the park.
examples.zh: 在公园散步后，她说：“「我们应该多这样聚聚」。”

examples.en: As lunch ended, he laughed and said, “We should do this more often.”
examples.zh: 午饭吃完时，他笑着说：“「我们应该多这样聚聚」。”

collocations: I think we should do this more often
we should do this more often next term
honestly, we should do this more often

words.enDefinition: to send brief recorded messages to one another instead of talking live

examples.en: We started to swap voice notes because our schedules rarely lined up after graduation.
examples.zh: 毕业后时间很少对得上，我们就开始「互发语音消息」。

examples.en: My old school friends swap voice notes when someone has news we want to hear.
examples.zh: 有人有大家想听的消息时，以前的同学就会「互发语音消息」。

collocations: swap voice notes instead of calling

words.enDefinition: a series of messages where people post and respond to photos

examples.en: Our photo thread started with a picture of the first flat we shared.
examples.zh: 我们的「照片讨论串」从一张以前合住的第一套公寓的照片开始。

examples.en: I found the campus picture in a photo thread my classmates had started.
examples.zh: 我在同学发起的一个「照片讨论串」里找到了那张校园照片。

words.enDefinition: a collection of photos several people are allowed to view or add to

examples.en: We made a shared photo album after the last trip of our exchange year.
examples.zh: 交换学年最后一次出游后，我们建了一个「共享相册」。

examples.en: A former classmate added an old picnic photo to our shared photo album.
examples.zh: 一位老同学往「共享相册」里加了一张以前野餐的照片。

collocations: add to a shared photo album
invite someone to a shared photo album

words.enDefinition: a brief account of important recent changes in someone's personal life

examples.en: My roommate sent a life update after she moved away for graduate school.
examples.zh: 室友搬去外地读研后，发来了一段「生活近况分享」。

examples.en: We each gave a short life update at the beginning of our monthly call.
examples.zh: 每月电话开始时，我们每个人都简短做了「生活近况分享」。

words.enDefinition: to share new information with the members of a group

examples.en: I offered to update the group after hearing from our friend about her flight.
examples.zh: 听到朋友的航班消息后，我主动提出「把进展告诉群里的人」。

examples.en: Will you update the group once you have spoken to our old classmate today?
examples.zh: 你今天和老同学谈过后，会「把进展告诉群里的人」吗？

collocations: send a message to update the group

words.enDefinition: an informal occasion when several people spend time together

examples.en: The afternoon turned into a group hangout after two classmates stopped by the café.
examples.zh: 两位同学来咖啡馆坐坐后，那个下午变成了「一帮朋友的休闲聚会」。

examples.en: I booked the common room for a group hangout before everyone left for summer.
examples.zh: 大家放暑假走之前，我订了公共休息室办「一帮朋友的休闲聚会」。

words.enDefinition: to fail to include someone in a group or shared activity

examples.en: I didn't want to leave someone out when I wrote invitations to our old classmates.
examples.zh: 给老同学写邀请时，我不想「把谁漏掉」。

examples.en: It can hurt to leave someone out of a conversation without noticing it.
examples.zh: 无意中「把某人排除在谈话之外」，也可能伤到对方。

collocations: leave someone out of the conversation

words.enDefinition: to give each person in a group a place in an activity or decision

examples.en: We tried to include everyone when we made plans around people's different class schedules.
examples.zh: 安排活动时，我们考虑了不同课表，尽量「把每个人都包括进来」。

examples.en: They wanted to include everyone in the photo before people left for the station.
examples.zh: 在有人去车站前，他们想把「每个人都拍进」照片里。

collocations: find a way to include everyone

words.enDefinition: to feel pressured between people who are disagreeing with each other

examples.en: I began to feel caught in the middle when both friends wanted my opinion.
examples.zh: 两个朋友都问我的看法，我开始「觉得夹在双方中间」。

examples.en: She told me it's easy to feel caught in the middle when flatmates argue.
examples.zh: 她跟我说，室友吵架时很容易「觉得夹在双方中间」。

collocations: start to feel caught in the middle
often feel caught in the middle
try not to feel caught in the middle

words.enDefinition: to get the wrong idea about each other's words or intentions

examples.en: Friends sometimes have a misunderstanding when they talk about serious things by text.
examples.zh: 朋友用文字聊严肃事情时，有时会「彼此产生误会」。

examples.en: I thought we might have a misunderstanding, so I asked what she meant.
examples.zh: 我想我们可能「彼此产生误会」了，就问她是什么意思。

collocations: have a misunderstanding with a friend

words.enDefinition: a quarrel that makes an established relationship unfriendly

examples.en: Their falling-out started over a small misunderstanding after the group moved flats.
examples.zh: 那群人搬家后，一点小误会让他们「闹翻」了。

examples.en: They had a falling-out early that year but still shared several friends on campus.
examples.zh: 那年年初他们「闹翻」了，但在校园里还有几个共同的朋友。

words.enDefinition: the ending of a close friendship, sometimes as a deliberate choice

examples.en: She found the friendship breakup harder to explain than moving to a different campus.
examples.zh: 她觉得「友情破裂」比转到另一个校区更难向别人解释。

examples.en: A friendship breakup changed who I talked to after our weekly seminar that year.
examples.zh: 那年一次「友情破裂」改变了我每周研讨课下课后会和谁聊天。

words.enDefinition: to remain neutral when people you know are in a disagreement

examples.en: I tried to avoid taking sides because I cared about both of my friends.
examples.zh: 我在乎两个朋友，所以尽量「避免偏向任何一方」。

examples.en: The club organiser chose to avoid taking sides in a disagreement about the venue.
examples.zh: 在关于场地的分歧中，社团组织者选择「避免偏向任何一方」。

words.enDefinition: to unfairly give certain people more attention or better treatment than others

examples.en: I worried that the organiser might play favourites when choosing who led each activity.
examples.zh: 我担心组织者在选每项活动的带领人时会「偏袒某些人」。

examples.en: She didn't want to play favourites between her two groups of friends at university.
examples.zh: 她不想在大学两群朋友之间「偏袒某些人」。

words.enDefinition: to put pressure on a friendship so it becomes harder to get along

examples.en: A series of missed calls can strain a friendship when both people are busy.
examples.zh: 两个人都忙时，一连串没接到的电话可能会「让友情变得紧张」。

examples.en: I didn't want the disagreement to strain a friendship that mattered to both of us.
examples.zh: 这段友情对我们俩都很重要，我不想分歧「让友情变得紧张」。

collocations: be enough to strain a friendship
avoid doing things that strain a friendship

words.enDefinition: to resolve problems or confusion through discussion or action

examples.en: We met for coffee to sort things out after the group chat became confusing.
examples.zh: 群聊说不清楚后，我们见面喝咖啡，好「把问题处理妥当」。

examples.en: The two friends needed time to sort things out after the summer plans changed.
examples.zh: 暑假计划改变后，那两位朋友需要时间「把问题处理妥当」。

words.enDefinition: to decide together to start again without carrying a previous dispute into the future

examples.en: They chose to agree to a fresh start after clearing up the old misunderstanding.
examples.zh: 说开旧误会后，两人选择「同意重新开始相处」。

examples.en: We could agree to a fresh start once we both felt ready to talk.
examples.zh: 等两人都准备好谈一谈，我们就可以「同意重新开始相处」。

collocations: decide to agree to a fresh start
be ready to agree to a fresh start
choose to agree to a fresh start

words.enDefinition: to take steps to improve a relationship after a disagreement

examples.en: I hoped we could patch things up before we went back to our seminar.
examples.zh: 我希望回去上研讨课前，我们能「修补彼此的关系」。

examples.en: They met at the library café to patch things up after avoiding each other all week.
examples.zh: 互相躲了一周后，他们在图书馆咖啡馆见面，想「修补彼此的关系」。

words.enDefinition: to improve a friendship hurt by conflict, distance, or lost trust

examples.en: It took time to mend a friendship after so much had been left unsaid.
examples.zh: 有那么多事没说开，「修复一段友情」需要时间。

examples.en: She wrote a private note because she wanted to mend a friendship from first year.
examples.zh: 她想「修复一段大一时的友情」，就私下写了张字条。

collocations: find ways to mend a friendship

words.enDefinition: to restore the ability to trust someone after it was damaged

examples.en: We knew it would take time to rebuild trust after the message was shared.
examples.zh: 消息被传开后，我们知道「重建信任」要时间。

examples.en: I wanted to rebuild trust by following through on the plans we made together.
examples.zh: 我想兑现一起定下的计划，好「重建信任」。

words.enDefinition: to let someone try again after a mistake or disappointment

examples.en: It can be hard to give someone a second chance after a broken promise.
examples.zh: 承诺被违背后，要「再给对方一次机会」并不容易。

examples.en: She felt ready to give someone a second chance after hearing both accounts.
examples.zh: 听了双方的说法后，她愿意「再给对方一次机会」。

collocations: decide to give someone a second chance
be willing to give someone a second chance
choose to give someone a second chance

words.enDefinition: to agree to stop dwelling on an old disagreement or wrong

examples.en: My former flatmate wanted to let bygones be bygones when we met again downtown.
examples.zh: 又在市中心见面时，原来的室友希望「过去的事就让它过去」。

examples.en: We decided to let bygones be bygones before planning a reunion together that spring.
examples.zh: 那年春天一起筹划聚会前，我们决定「过去的事就让它过去」。

collocations: decide to let bygones be bygones
agree to let bygones be bygones
ready to let bygones be bygones

words.enDefinition: to settle an old quarrel and get on better with someone

examples.en: The two friends agreed to bury the hatchet before their classmates visited that weekend.
examples.zh: 周末同学来访前，那两位朋友同意「结束长期争执」。

examples.en: I thought it was time to bury the hatchet after months of awkward silence.
examples.zh: 尴尬地不说话好几个月后，我觉得该「结束长期争执」了。

words.enDefinition: to do something to repair the harm caused by a mistake

examples.en: He tried to make amends by inviting everyone he had left out before.
examples.zh: 他邀请了之前被自己漏掉的所有人，试着「做点事弥补过失」。

examples.en: I wanted to make amends after realising my joke had embarrassed a friend.
examples.zh: 意识到自己的玩笑让朋友难堪后，我想「做点事弥补过失」。

words.enDefinition: willing to talk to each other after an argument or other difficulty

examples.en: We were still on speaking terms even after our argument over the train tickets.
examples.zh: 即便为火车票吵过，两人也「还愿意彼此说话」。

examples.en: I didn't know they were not on speaking terms when I planned the dinner.
examples.zh: 安排晚餐时，我不知道两人「已经不愿意彼此说话了」。

words.enDefinition: to bring back a friendship that has grown weaker or been inactive

examples.en: They used their old film club to rekindle a friendship after years of silence.
examples.zh: 多年没联系后，两人借原来的电影社活动「重新培养一段友情」。

examples.en: I wanted to rekindle a friendship but didn't know how to start the conversation.
examples.zh: 我想「重新培养一段友情」，却不知怎样开口。

collocations: a chance to rekindle a friendship

words.enDefinition: to correct a misunderstanding about what really happened

examples.en: I wrote to set the record straight after hearing a different story from classmates.
examples.zh: 从同学那里听到另一种说法后，我发消息想「把事实澄清」。

examples.en: She asked for a moment to set the record straight before the group finished talking.
examples.zh: 大家还没聊完，她就希望占用一点时间「把事实澄清」。

collocations: want to set the record straight
take time to set the record straight
try to set the record straight

words.enDefinition: to deliberately reduce how closely you spend time or communicate with a friend

examples.en: She said it can be hard to distance yourself from a friend you still admire.
examples.zh: 她说，要「主动和自己仍欣赏的朋友拉开距离」可能很难。

examples.en: My tutor asked what it meant to distance yourself from a friend without being rude.
examples.zh: 导师问，「主动和朋友拉开距离」而又不失礼，是怎样一回事。

collocations: choose to distance yourself from a friend
start to distance yourself from a friend
find it difficult to distance yourself from a friend

words.enDefinition: to allow a friendship to become weaker through increasingly little contact

examples.en: I didn't want to let a friendship fade just because my timetable became busy.
examples.zh: 我不想只因课表忙起来就「任由友情淡下来」。

examples.en: She wondered whether she had started to let a friendship fade without meaning to.
examples.zh: 她在想，自己是不是已经无意间「任由友情淡下来」。

collocations: decide to let a friendship fade
try not to let a friendship fade
allow yourself to let a friendship fade

words.enDefinition: to contact someone again after a period without communication

examples.en: We decided to get back in touch after realising we lived in the same city.
examples.zh: 发现住在同一座城后，我们决定「重新联系上」。

examples.en: An old classmate wanted to get back in touch after seeing a graduation photograph.
examples.zh: 一位老同学看到毕业照后想「重新联系上」。

collocations: try to get back in touch
decide to get back in touch
get back in touch with someone

words.enDefinition: a gathering where former students of a university or school meet again

examples.en: I registered for the alumni reunion after finding out my old roommate was coming.
examples.zh: 得知老室友也会来后，我报名参加了「校友聚会」。

examples.en: The campus tour at the alumni reunion included the library we used every weekend.
examples.zh: 「校友聚会」的校园参观包括我们以前每周末都去的图书馆。

words.enDefinition: an organized meeting of people who attended the same school class or graduating year

examples.en: The class reunion gave us a chance to hear where everyone had ended up.
examples.zh: 「同学聚会」让我们有机会了解大家后来都去了哪里。

examples.en: I saw three friends from my first year at the class reunion that summer.
examples.zh: 那年夏天的「同学聚会」上，我见到了三个大一时的朋友。

words.enDefinition: a weekend set aside for people who have been apart to meet again

examples.en: We booked our train tickets for the reunion weekend before the cheap seats sold out.
examples.zh: 便宜座位卖光之前，我们订了「聚会周末」的火车票。

examples.en: Our reunion weekend began with a walk through the neighbourhood where we used to live.
examples.zh: 我们在以前住的街区散了个步，拉开了「聚会周末」的序幕。

words.enDefinition: a gathering held to say goodbye to someone who is leaving

examples.en: We organized a farewell party for our flatmate before her flight back home.
examples.zh: 室友乘机回家前，我们为她安排了一场「送别聚会」。

examples.en: My old study group met for a farewell party in the common room.
examples.zh: 我原来的学习小组在公共休息室办了一场「送别聚会」。

words.enDefinition: a written or spoken message wishing someone well as they leave

examples.en: We recorded a farewell message for a friend who couldn't attend our dinner.
examples.zh: 我们为没法来聚餐的朋友录了一段「告别留言」。

examples.en: My classmate left a farewell message in the notebook we'd been sharing all year.
examples.zh: 同学在那本我们共用了一整年的笔记本里留了段「告别留言」。

words.expression: let me know how it goes
words.lemma: let me know how it goes
words.enDefinition: a request for someone to share the outcome of something they are doing
acceptedEnVariants: let me know how it goes

examples.en: “Let me know how it goes,” she said as I left for the interview.
examples.zh: 我出发去面试时，她说：“「告诉我后来怎么样」。”

examples.en: I wrote, “Let me know how it goes when you meet your new supervisor.”
examples.zh: 我写道：“见过新导师后，「告诉我后来怎么样」。”

collocations: let me know how it goes tomorrow
please let me know how it goes
let me know how it goes after your appointment

words.expression: all the best for the move
words.lemma: all the best for the move
words.enDefinition: a friendly wish that someone's upcoming move goes well
acceptedEnVariants: all the best for the move
all the best with the move

examples.en: “All the best for the move,” he wrote on the card from our flat.
examples.zh: 他在我们公寓的卡片上写道：“「祝你搬家顺利」。”

examples.en: We said all the best for the move before her taxi left for the station.
examples.zh: 她的出租车开去车站前，我们说：“「祝你搬家顺利」。”

collocations: wish someone all the best for the move
a message saying all the best for the move
all the best for the move next week

words.enDefinition: an informal request to stay in contact or visit again after leaving

examples.en: “Don't be a stranger,” my old tutor said as I left the department.
examples.zh: 我离开系里时，以前的导师说：“「以后别断了联系」。”

examples.en: My friend waved and said, “Don't be a stranger when you're back in town.”
examples.zh: 朋友挥手说：“回来时记得来找我，「别断了联系」。”

collocations: don't be a stranger after graduation
don't be a stranger when you're nearby

words.expression: drop by when you're in town
words.lemma: drop by when you're in town
words.enDefinition: an informal invitation to visit when the other person is nearby
acceptedEnVariants: drop by when you're in town

examples.en: “Drop by when you're in town next week,” she said after the reunion.
examples.zh: 聚会结束后，她说：“下周「进城时顺道过来」。”

examples.en: I wrote, “Drop by when you're in town, and we'll get dinner together.”
examples.zh: 我写道：“「进城时顺道过来」，我们一起吃晚饭。”

collocations: feel free to drop by when you're in town
do drop by when you're in town
drop by when you're in town next

words.enDefinition: an assurance that someone is welcome to return or visit in future

examples.en: “You're always welcome here,” my former neighbours told me before I left for university.
examples.zh: 我出发去上学前，以前的邻居跟我说：“「随时欢迎你来」。”

examples.en: My friend said, “You're always welcome here if your new city feels lonely sometimes.”
examples.zh: 朋友说：“在新城市有时觉得孤单的话，「随时欢迎你来」。”

collocations: know that you're always welcome here

words.enDefinition: to part from someone while expecting to see or speak to them again

examples.en: We stopped by the old café to say goodbye for now before her train.
examples.zh: 她坐火车前，我们顺路去老咖啡馆「先道个别」。

examples.en: I knew we'd have to say goodbye for now after the final reunion lunch.
examples.zh: 我知道重聚的最后一顿午饭结束后，我们得「先道个别」。

collocations: come to say goodbye for now
take a moment to say goodbye for now
wave and say goodbye for now

words.enDefinition: to mail a card with a picture and a short written message

examples.en: I promised to send a postcard from the city where I was studying abroad.
examples.zh: 我答应从自己留学的城市「寄一张明信片」。

examples.en: She wanted to send a postcard instead of only sharing photos in the chat.
examples.zh: 她想「寄一张明信片」，不只在群聊里分享照片。

collocations: send a postcard to a friend

words.enDefinition: to make communication or relationships feel closer despite physical distance

examples.en: Weekly calls helped bridge the distance after we moved to three separate countries.
examples.zh: 我们搬到三个不同国家后，每周的电话帮助我们「拉近彼此的距离」。

examples.en: The shared album was another way to bridge the distance between old university friends.
examples.zh: 共享相册也能帮助大学老友「拉近彼此的距离」。

collocations: find ways to bridge the distance
use video calls to bridge the distance

words.enDefinition: easily reachable by telephone whenever someone needs you

examples.en: My sister said she was just a phone call away during my first semester.
examples.zh: 姐姐说，我第一学期有事「打个电话就能联系到她」。

examples.en: It helped to know that my old roommate was still just a phone call away.
examples.zh: 知道以前的室友仍然「打个电话就能联系到」，让我安心。

collocations: remember I'm just a phone call away
always just a phone call away

words.enDefinition: to look at different people's calendars to find suitable shared times

examples.en: We needed to compare calendars before setting a date for our next group call.
examples.zh: 定下一次群组通话的日期前，我们得「对一对各自的日程」。

examples.en: I suggested we compare calendars after everyone had received their new timetables for spring.
examples.zh: 大家都收到春季新课表后，我建议「对一对各自的日程」。

words.enDefinition: a time set aside to exchange news after a period without seeing each other

examples.en: We planned a catch-up session after the lecture for people from our old project.
examples.zh: 讲座后我们给以前项目组的人安排了一个「专门聊近况的聚会」。

examples.en: The catch-up session lasted until the café turned off the music that evening.
examples.zh: 那晚，这次「专门聊近况的聚会」一直持续到咖啡馆关掉音乐。

words.enDefinition: to receive a message or other contact from a friend from the past

examples.en: It's always nice to hear from an old friend when a long term ends.
examples.zh: 漫长的一个学期结束时，「收到老朋友的消息」总让人开心。

examples.en: I didn't expect to hear from an old friend the week after our class reunion.
examples.zh: 我没想到同学聚会后一周就会「收到老朋友的消息」。

collocations: be glad to hear from an old friend
hope to hear from an old friend
surprised to hear from an old friend

words.enDefinition: a friendly expression used when speaking to someone you have missed

examples.en: “It's good to hear your voice again,” she said when our call finally connected.
examples.zh: 电话终于接通了，她说：“再次「听到你的声音真好」。”

examples.en: I said, “It's good to hear your voice,” before asking about her new flat.
examples.zh: 我说：“「听到你的声音真好」。”然后问起了她的新公寓。

collocations: so good to hear your voice
it's good to hear your voice again
good to hear your voice after so long

words.expression: we haven't seen each other in years
words.lemma: we haven't seen each other in years
words.enDefinition: a phrase saying two people have gone several years without meeting
acceptedEnVariants: we haven't seen each other in years

examples.en: She said, “We haven't seen each other in years,” when I arrived at the station.
examples.zh: 我到车站时，她说：“「我们好多年没见了」。”

examples.en: “We haven't seen each other in years, but we still talk every month online.”
examples.zh: “「我们好多年没见了」，不过每月还是在线上聊天。”

collocations: we haven't seen each other in years but still text
realise we haven't seen each other in years
we haven't seen each other in years now

words.enDefinition: feeling so familiar that a long absence barely seems noticeable

examples.en: Back in the old café, it felt like we never left after that summer.
examples.zh: 回到老咖啡馆时，暑假过后感觉「就像我们没离开过」。

examples.en: We started telling the same jokes again, like we never left the residence hall.
examples.zh: 我们又讲起同样的笑话，「就像我们没离开过」宿舍楼。

collocations: it was like we never left

words.enDefinition: to be unaware of what a group has been discussing or doing

examples.en: I felt I might be out of the loop after missing three group calls.
examples.zh: 错过三次群组通话后，我觉得自己可能「没跟上大家的近况」。

examples.en: She didn't want to be out of the loop while studying at another campus.
examples.zh: 她在另一个校区读书时，不想「没跟上大家的近况」。

collocations: seem to be out of the loop
not want to be out of the loop
friends who might be out of the loop

words.enDefinition: a phrase saying someone is mentioned during a conversation

examples.en: His name comes up whenever we talk about our first month in the residence.
examples.zh: 我们一聊起刚住宿舍的第一个月，「就有人提到他的名字」。

examples.en: Her name comes up a lot when the old group gets together for coffee.
examples.zh: 老朋友聚着喝咖啡时，「经常有人提到她的名字」。

collocations: someone's name comes up in conversation
his name comes up at reunions

words.enDefinition: to share a number of difficult or important experiences over time

examples.en: Friends can go through a lot together during the final year of a demanding course.
examples.zh: 一门很难的课程最后一年，朋友们可能「一起经历很多事」。

examples.en: We knew we'd go through a lot together when our placements began in different places.
examples.zh: 我们知道，实习在不同地方开始后，两人会「一起经历很多事」。

collocations: go through a lot together at university
friends who go through a lot together
expect to go through a lot together

words.expression: be part of each other's lives
words.lemma: be part of each other's lives
words.enDefinition: to remain involved in what happens to another person over time
acceptedEnVariants: be part of each other's lives

examples.en: We wanted to be part of each other's lives after moving to separate cities.
examples.zh: 搬到不同城市后，我们还是想「参与彼此的生活」。

examples.en: Sharing our small successes helped us be part of each other's lives from afar.
examples.zh: 分享小小的成就，让我们即使相隔很远，也能「参与彼此的生活」。

collocations: continue to be part of each other's lives
find ways to be part of each other's lives
want to be part of each other's lives

words.enDefinition: to say goodbye to someone in a friendly or celebratory way as they leave

examples.en: Our study group met to give a warm send-off to two exchange students.
examples.zh: 我们学习小组碰面「热情送别」两名交换生。

examples.en: The club planned to give a warm send-off to its graduating members that evening.
examples.zh: 社团打算那晚给即将毕业的成员「热情送行」。

collocations: give a warm send-off to friends
gather to give a warm send-off
plan to give a warm send-off

words.expression: make it back for the reunion
words.lemma: make it back for the reunion
words.enDefinition: to be able to return in time for a gathering with people from your past
acceptedEnVariants: make it back for the reunion

examples.en: I hope you can make it back for the reunion before your work term starts.
examples.zh: 希望你工作学期开始前能「赶回去参加聚会」。

examples.en: My old classmate couldn't make it back for the reunion because her train was cancelled.
examples.zh: 火车取消了，老同学没能「赶回去参加聚会」。

collocations: hope to make it back for the reunion
try to make it back for the reunion
be able to make it back for the reunion
